newsitem.title: KENYA: Zairean rebel leader waits in Cabinda.
newsitem.headline: Zairean rebel leader waits in Cabinda.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila has gone to the Angolan enclave of Cabinda on his way to meet President Mobutu Sese Seko on the South African navy ship Outeniqua off Congo, a rebel official said on Wednesday.

"The president (Kabila) is in Cabinda waiting. He wants to go to the ship but the ship is still in Pointe Noire (in Congo) and it must be in international waters," the official told Reuters by telephone from Cabinda.
Cabinda is 80 km (50 miles) south of Pointe Noire, in a part of Angola separated from the rest of the country by Zaire's narrow corridor to the sea.
President Mobutu and South African President Nelson Mandela, who has been mediating between Mobutu and the rebels, arrived in Congo on Wednesday for the meeting.
A first meeting between Mobutu and Kabila on May 4 ended inconclusively. Mobutu offered to hand power to a transitional authority but Kabila insisted he take power directly.
Kabila's aides have said they are going to the second meeting in the expectation that Mobutu, who has lost control of most of Zaire, will now comply with their demands.
